plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for ZTE ZXR10 switch. It reports uptime, CPU utilization, memory utilization, temperature, fan, power supply status, and interface traffic (enterprise PEN 3902).
name: Switch

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage
metrics.description: This metric reports the CPU utilization of the ZTE ZXR10 device control plane (ZXR10-MIB zxr10SystemCpuUtility5m, five-minute average), averaged across units and normalized to 0-100. Sustained high CPU usage can indicate control-plane overload, routing instability, or attack traffic, and may lead to slow management response or packet processing delays.

metrics.name: device_memory_total
metrics.description: This metric reports the total size in bytes of the ZTE ZXR10 unit memory (ZXR10-MIB zxr10SystemMemSize). Together with the used octets it determines overall memory utilization.

metrics.name: device_memory_used
metrics.description: This metric reports the number of octets currently in use by the ZTE ZXR10 unit memory (ZXR10-MIB zxr10SystemMemUsed). It is an absolute used-byte value, not a percent-used reading. It helps administrators understand absolute memory consumption and identify when the device is under memory pressure.

metrics.name: device_memory_usage
metrics.description: This metric reports overall memory utilization of the ZTE ZXR10 device, computed as used / total * 100 from zxr10SystemMemUsed (octets) and zxr10SystemMemSize (bytes). High memory usage may indicate memory leaks, oversized routing/MAC/ARP tables, or insufficient capacity, and can cause instability or failed allocations.

metrics.name: device_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: This metric reports the board temperature in degrees Celsius of each ZTE ZXR10 slot (ZXR10-MIB zxr10SlotTemperature). Abnormally high temperatures may indicate fan failure, blocked airflow, or excessive ambient heat, and can trigger thermal protection or hardware damage if left unaddressed.

metrics.name: device_fan_state
metrics.description: This metric reports the operational state of each ZTE ZXR10 cooling fan (POWERFANS-MIB fanStat, raw 0=online / 1=offline), normalized via telegraf processors.enum so that 1 = healthy and 2 = fault. A value greater than 1 indicates a cooling fault that can quickly lead to overheating and should be investigated immediately.

metrics.name: device_psu_state
metrics.description: This metric reports the operational state of each ZTE ZXR10 power supply (POWERFANS-MIB powerStat, raw 0=work / 1=online / 2=offline), normalized via telegraf processors.enum so that 1 = healthy (work or online) and 2 = fault. A non-normal state signals a power redundancy or hardware fault; on devices with redundant PSUs a single failure may not cause an outage but removes redundancy and must be remediated promptly.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes received over the past 5 minutes, measured in bytes per second, from the 64-bit IF-MIB ifHCInOctets counter (ifXTable). The 64-bit counter avoids the rapid wrap of the 32-bit ifInOctets on high-speed switch ports, keeping the rate accurate.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric calculates the average rate of bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, measured in bytes per second, from the 64-bit IF-MIB ifHCOutOctets counter (ifXTable). The 64-bit counter avoids the rapid wrap of the 32-bit ifOutOctets on high-speed switch ports, keeping the rate accurate.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
